intended_object: The rank-one structure carried by a discrete (rank-one, ℤ-valued) valuation: an order-preserving embedding of its value group into ℝ≥0, here normalized so that a uniformizer has value e⁻¹ for a chosen base e > 1 (i.e. |x| = e^{-ord(x)}). Inferred from the docstring and the module doc ("Discrete valuations have rank one").
explanation:
The definition builds the map `hom'` in two steps. First, `valueGroup₀_equiv_withZeroMulInt` is the order isomorphism from `v.ValueGroup₀` to ℤᵐ⁰. It sends the generator γ (which is < 1) to `exp(-1)`. Second, `WithZeroMulInt.toNNReal` sends `exp n` to eⁿ and 0 to 0. This second map is a monoid-with-zero hom, and it is strictly monotone when e > 1.

So the composite is a strictly monotone monoid-with-zero hom from the value group to ℝ≥0, sending γ^k to e^{-k}. That is the standard normalized embedding of a discrete valuation into ℝ≥0. The proof of `exists_val_nontrivial` comes from `IsNontrivial`, which is part of `IsRankOneDiscrete`.

The base e is a free parameter, as in the literature: the absolute value attached to a discrete valuation is only defined up to the choice of e (for example e = q, the residue field size, for local fields).

The generality is natural: any ring R and any linearly ordered commutative group with zero Γ. A general existence result appears in the same RankOne file (`nonempty_rankOne_iff_mulArchimedean`), but it only gives a `Nonempty` (a proof that some structure exists), not this explicit normalized data. So this definition does not duplicate an existing Mathlib definition. It is faithful.
